diagnosed_root_cause.physical_consequence: The delegated service cgroup still contained the trusted controller process. cgroup v2's no-internal-process constraint therefore forbade the parent from distributing memory or pids to any child, so cgroup.subtree_control stayed empty and the first real EffectCgroup.create() failed with EACCES after readiness had already promised CGROUP_V2_AND_RLIMIT.
diagnosed_root_cause.summary: probe_cgroup_delegation() was a false-positive readiness probe: it proved only that an empty child directory could be created and removed inside the delegated cgroup, then reported available=true.
what_the_probe_did_not_prove: the trusted controller is outside the delegated parent
the parent satisfies the cgroup-v2 no-internal-process constraint
memory and pids are enabled in cgroup.subtree_control
a real effect cgroup receives memory.max and pids.max
those values are readable back from the kernel
a gated child can be attached and verified before exec

ending_commit_note: The ending commit is the single intentional commit 'fix: qualify paired runner cgroup topology' created on this branch; its hash is reported in the terminal response and cannot appear inside the object it commits.
environment_limitations: The development controller process runs in /sys/fs/cgroup/init.scope, where an unprivileged manager leaf cannot be created (EACCES), so probe_cgroup_delegation() reports MANAGER_LEAF_CREATE_FAILED and the delegated physical tests skip honestly without ADMISSIBLE_REQUIRE_DELEGATED_CGROUP=1
The implementation agent has no interactive sudo access, so the delegated physical module must be run by the operator inside a transient Delegate=yes systemd unit

topology.description: delegated service cgroup (effect parent) -> { trusted manager leaf holding the controller process, one sibling effect cgroup per effect holding the gated launcher and command process tree }
